entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aurelian of Réôme (800-850 CE) was a Frankish writer and music theorist who made a lasting impact on medieval Europe. Born in Réôme, a small town in the Frankish Kingdom, he would go on to author the Musica disciplina, the earliest extant treatise on music from medieval Europe.

As a prominent figure in the medieval intellectual landscape, Aurelian's work reflected the cultural and artistic trends of the time. His emphasis on the importance of rhythm and melody in music helped shape the development of Western classical music. The Musica disciplina's influence can be seen in the works of later composers, such as Hildegard von Bingen and Guillaume de Machaut.

Aurelian's legacy extends beyond the world of music. His writings on the nature of beauty and the role of art in society demonstrate his intellectual curiosity and his ability to engage with the broader cultural and philosophical debates of his time. Today, Aurelian of Réôme is recognized as a key figure in the history of Western classical music and a testament to the enduring power of artistic expression.

In the words of musicologist, Hans Tischler, 'Aurelian of Réôme's contribution to the development of Western classical music is a testament to the enduring power of human creativity and the importance of understanding the cultural and historical context in which it arises.'
